svg.text: ESP32 main board on a half-size ElectroCookie solderable breadboard
Top view. ESP32-DevKitC (38-pin, WROOM-32U) on two 19-pin female headers in rows a and i, USB toward column 1.
The shaded outline is the raised ESP32. Parts and wires under it (dashed) go in first, before the ESP32 is plugged into its headers.
2 × 19-pin: row a cols 1–19 and row i cols 1–19. Check the ESP32 drops in before soldering them.
R1 10k: c10 ↔ c6 (GPIO26 to the GND pin), lying flat.
b19 → top 3V3 rail @ 21 · e10 → e22 (GPIO26) · d11 → d25 (GPIO25) · c15 → c27 (GPIO34)
g14 → g23 (SDA) · h17 → h24 (SCL) · 5V wire to cutoff board soldered in b1, run out past the USB end
j13 → bottom GND @ 13 · j19 → bottom GND @ 19 · f23 → f25 (SDA) · i24 → i26 (SCL)
top GND @ 29 → bottom GND @ 29 · top 3V3 @ 30 → bottom 3V3 @ 30
solder each wire into the hole shown at its label (table at right); then plug in the ESP32
5V b1 · GND top GND rail @ 23 · PERMIT a25 · FB a27 · HB j18
VCC bottom 3V3 rail @ 20 · GND bottom GND rail @ 21 · SDA j23 · SCL j24
SDA j25 · SCL j26 · 3V3 bottom 3V3 rail @ 27 · GND bottom GND rail @ 28
VCC bottom 3V3 rail @ 12 · SDA j14 · GND bottom GND rail @ 15 · SCL j17
VCC bottom 3V3 rail @ 5 · GND bottom GND rail @ 6 · DAT j7
DAT j8 · VCC bottom 3V3 rail @ 9 · GND bottom GND rail @ 10
• Fit a 2.4 GHz U.FL antenna to the WROOM-32U socket (the module has no antenna of its own). A pigtail lets the antenna sit outside the project box.
• The DS18B20 adapter boards already carry the 4.7k pull-ups, so DAT wires go straight to the ESP32 pins. The OLED and IR boards supply the I2C pull-ups.
• Only ESP32 GND pins on the right side (13, 19) reach the rails; the left GND pin is used just for R1. They are joined inside the ESP32.
• Power comes from USB on the ESP32. Measure 3.3 V across the top rails and ~5 V at the cutoff 5V wire before connecting sensors.
• Cutoff wires (5V, GND, HB, PERMIT, FB) go to J1 on the cutoff board: f2 5V, f3 GND, f4 HB, f5 PERMIT, f6 FB.
